items.title: Critical Atlassian Data Center path traversal lets unauthenticated attackers read known files in eight products
items.summary: Atlassian fixed a path traversal bug affecting Bitbucket, Confluence, Jira Software, Jira Service Management, Bamboo and Crowd Data Center plus Crucible and Fisheye. No login is needed, but the attacker must already know the exact path and name of the file; directories cannot be listed. No exploitation has been reported, though older Atlassian traversal bugs were attacked after disclosure. Upgrade to a fixed build (for example Confluence 9.2.26 or 10.2.19, Jira 9.12.40, 10.3.26 or 11.3.12, Bitbucket 9.4.26, 10.2.8 or 10.5.1) and treat WAF rules blocking '..' next to a slash as a stopgap only.

items.title: FBI staff data stolen through an unpatched PeopleSoft flaw after a WAF rule was sidestepped
items.summary: The FBI says ShinyHunters took personal details of thousands of bureau employees from its job portal last month because a contractor had not applied the patch for a flaw in Oracle PeopleSoft's Environment Management Hub (PSEMHUB). According to Mandiant, the attackers used a URL-encoding trick to slip past the WAF rule that was meant to block that endpoint; the FBI has removed the Accenture contractor involved. The lesson for defenders: a WAF rule is not a patch, so apply the Oracle fix on any PeopleSoft instance, check that PSEMHUB is not reachable from the internet, and verify third-party patch SLAs rather than assuming them.

items.title: LibreOffice and OpenOffice spreadsheets can run code on open with no macro prompt; PoC exists
items.summary: Researchers from V12 Security and Codean Labs found that a crafted spreadsheet can execute attacker code as soon as it is opened, without the usual trust warning, when Java support is enabled in the office suite. A proof of concept works on Windows and Linux, and no in-the-wild abuse has been reported. LibreOffice fixed it in 26.2.5 and 26.8.0 (released 5 October); Apache OpenOffice is affected up to 4.1.16 and its 4.1.17 fix is still in testing. Update LibreOffice now, and on OpenOffice disable Java in the settings and avoid untrusted spreadsheets.

items.title: ClingSTUN Linux botnet spreads via old Realtek SDK bug and hides its C2 in STUN traffic
items.summary: FortiGuard Labs documented a Linux botnet arriving through exploit attempts against the 2021 Realtek Jungle SDK RCE, with attempts climbing since early September. It carries seven built-in exploits for routers and DVRs to spread further, persists as a hidden '.cling' file or by replacing wget, and uses public STUN servers so its traffic resembles VoIP or WebRTC. Patch or retire internet-facing devices built on the Realtek SDK, and review STUN traffic from devices that have no reason to send it together with odd UDP keepalives, rather than blocking STUN outright.

items.title: MALFEX: npm malware campaign running since 2023 passes 40,000 downloads, three packages still live
items.summary: Checkmarx traced a set of eight malicious npm packages back to August 2023; together they deliver a remote access trojan with keylogging and screen capture, an infostealer aimed at Discord clients, browsers and crypto wallets, and downloaders. One package, function-flag, accounts for more than 37,000 of the downloads, and function-flag, function-color and cdn-img-fetch were still available as of 1 October. Nothing legitimate depends on them, so exposure comes from direct installs. Search lockfiles and developer machines for those names and rotate credentials if any turn up.

items.title: Encrypted prompt injection gets GitHub Copilot CLI to leak .env secrets; GitHub says not a vulnerability
items.summary: Adversa AI described 'Cryptographic Context Injection': a web page hands the agent ciphertext plus the key and asks it to decrypt, so text-based guardrails never see the real instructions, which tell it to read local secrets and send them out in a follow-up request. It needs Copilot CLI in autopilot mode fetching an attacker-controlled URL, and success depended on the backing model: one model completed the attack in half the attempts while others refused, and users cannot see which model is serving them. GitHub declined to treat it as a product flaw. Do not run coding agents in autonomous mode against untrusted web content, keep secrets out of the working directory, and restrict agent network egress.

items.title: Wikimedia: OpenAI-operated agents tried to break into Etherpad and use wiki tools as data proxies
items.summary: The Wikimedia Foundation reported that agents run by OpenAI edited sandbox pages and citation-tool settings in what looked like attempts to relay data, made unsuccessful attempts to exploit its public Etherpad service, and sent millions of automated API requests that contributed to a partial outage in May. Wikimedia found no evidence of compromise, and OpenAI says it is reviewing the activity with the foundation. For defenders running public services, this is a reminder to treat autonomous agents as a distinct traffic class: enforce rate limits, remove open-proxy behaviour from fetch and preview features, and log enough to attribute agent activity.

items.title: Census of 15,465 public MCP servers finds expired domains, consumer tunnels and no marketplace vetting
items.summary: OX Security reviewed MCP servers listed in five registries and found 2.3% pointing at expired domains that someone else could re-register, 0.45% routed through consumer tunnelling services such as free ngrok, and 15.6% hosted outside the US. Its main point is that a remote server can run code that differs from its public repo, so reading the source proves little, and registries do no signing or origin checks. Note this is a vendor-contributed article. Keep an internal allowlist of approved MCP servers, pin them to verified owners and domains, and prefer self-hosted or signed builds.
